security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown links, template literals, CSS terms, and simulated typing language. Real risks are CDN dependencies, opaque media assets, and a package loader that can run npm and inherit environment variables.

remediation.issue: scripts/package-loader.mjs can run npm install and re-execute Node.
remediation.suggestion: Avoid automatic dependency bootstrap in marketplace skills, or require explicit user approval with clear package names, pinned versions, and no inherited secrets.

remediation.issue: The bootstrap child process inherits the full parent environment.
remediation.suggestion: Pass only the environment variables needed for Node execution and HyperFrames package resolution instead of spreading process.env.

remediation.issue: Examples and recipes load animation libraries from public CDNs.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer local, pinned dependencies or include integrity guidance so users can review third-party script sources before rendering examples.

remediation.issue: Bundled image and video assets are opaque to static scanning.
remediation.suggestion: Document asset provenance and scan media files with suitable binary and metadata tools before publishing.

content.value_statement: Complex HyperFrames scenes need deterministic motion that remains seek-safe during rendering. This skill supplies reusable motion rules, blueprints, transitions, and runtime adapters for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Selects atomic motion rules by trigger, visual role, and animation pattern.
Provides multi-phase scene blueprints with timing, constraints, and runnable HTML examples.
Explains adapters for GSAP, Lottie, Three.js, Anime.js, CSS animations, WAAPI, and TypeGPU.
Documents transition patterns for scene-to-scene motion in HyperFrames compositions.
Includes an animation-map script that inspects registered GSAP timelines and writes a choreography report.
limitations: It assumes the HyperFrames core rendering contract and does not replace hyperframes-core guidance.
Some runnable examples load animation libraries from public CDNs unless adapted to local dependencies.
The animation-map script may bootstrap a pinned HyperFrames producer package before running.
It provides recipes and examples, not a full visual editor or automatic design validator.

use_cases.title: Build product demo motion
use_cases.description: Use a blueprint to assemble a multi-phase demo scene with deterministic timing and reusable animation beats.

use_cases.title: Adapt runtime-specific animation code
use_cases.description: Reference the GSAP, Three.js, Lottie, Anime.js, CSS, WAAPI, or TypeGPU adapter for the correct API pattern.

use_cases.title: Audit animation choreography
use_cases.description: Run the animation-map workflow to inspect registered timelines, tween density, dead zones, and lifecycle warnings.

prompt_templates.title: Pick a motion rule
prompt_templates.prompt: Choose one HyperFrames animation rule for a short product metric reveal. Explain why it fits, list required elements, and note timing constraints.

prompt_templates.title: Compose a scene blueprint
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the HyperFrames animation blueprints to plan a four-phase SaaS feature demo. Include phase timing, chosen rules, and deterministic render constraints.

prompt_templates.title: Port to a runtime adapter
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this GSAP-based HyperFrames motion idea to the best runtime adapter. Preserve seek-safe timing, timeline registration, and deterministic state.

prompt_templates.title: Audit timeline quality
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this HyperFrames composition plan for animation risks. Identify timeline gaps, unsafe callbacks, layout measurement risks, and adapter-specific fixes.

output_examples.input: A prompt asks for a brand reveal with a typed companion line and a final hero zoom.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends the brand-reveal blueprint, combines discrete text sequencing with coordinate target zoom, and lists timing constraints for each phase.

output_examples.input: A prompt asks whether to use CSS keyframes, GSAP, or WAAPI for a simple shimmer loop.
output_examples.output: The skill compares the adapters, recommends CSS keyframes for decorative repeated motion, and warns against wall-clock JavaScript callbacks.

output_examples.input: A prompt asks for a choreography review after building a HyperFrames scene.
output_examples.output: The skill points to the animation-map script and describes the expected report sections: tween summaries, density, staggers, dead zones, and snapshots.

best_practices: Start with two to four atomic rules before loading a full scene blueprint.
Keep timelines paused, registered, deterministic, and driven by declared duration.
Use runtime adapters only when their strengths match the visual requirement.
anti_patterns: Do not create animation state from wall-clock time, random values, or render-time DOM measurements.
Do not combine multiple animation runtimes without registering each seekable timeline or instance.
Do not copy CDN examples into production without reviewing dependency sourcing and version pinning.

faq.question: Does this skill generate complete HyperFrames scenes?
faq.answer: It provides rules, recipes, and examples that help an agent author complete scenes. The final implementation still depends on the user prompt and project.

faq.question: Which runtime should I use by default?
faq.answer: Use GSAP for most HyperFrames motion because the rules and blueprints are built around paused timelines and precise seeking.

faq.question: Can it support 3D or shader-driven scenes?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Three.js, WebGL, HTML-as-texture, and TypeGPU guidance for 3D and GPU-rendered effects.

faq.question: Are the examples production-ready?
faq.answer: They are runnable references for animation behavior. Review assets, dependency loading, accessibility, and brand fit before production use.

faq.question: Does it replace hyperframes-core?
faq.answer: No. This skill assumes the core composition contract and adds animation-specific guidance on top of it.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The metadata declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code, and the content is written for agent-driven implementation.
